title: Affine Hopf algebra and module coaction data with coordinate linearizations
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra, with its comultiplication $\Delta$, counit $\epsilon$, and antipode $S$; in particular the coordinate algebra of an affine group scheme has this structure by [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. Let $E$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, and use tensor products and extension of scalars as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-module-base-change], with the commutative tensor algebra structure of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. An algebra coaction is a $k$-algebra map $\rho:E\to E\otimes_k C$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities. Put $L=E\otimes_k C$. For any $k$-algebra map $r:E\to L$, its extension module is $L\otimes_{E,r}M$, with $l\cdot(a\otimes m)=la\otimes m$, generating map $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, and induced module map $a\otimes m\mapsto a\otimes f(m)$. For any $E$-module $M$, give $M\otimes_k C$ the $L$-action $(e\otimes c)(m\otimes d)=em\otimes cd$. A module coaction over $\rho$ is a $k$-linear map $\theta:M\to M\otimes_k C$ satisfying $\theta(em)=\rho(e)\theta(m)$, $(1\otimes\epsilon)\theta=1_M$, and $(\theta\otimes1)\theta=(1\otimes\Delta)\theta$, with the standard tensor associativity and unit identifications. For any commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and map $r:E\to A$, write $A\otimes_{E,r}M$ for the actual scalar extension. Write $t(e)=e\otimes1$ and $u_L(e\otimes c)=e\epsilon(c)$. Put $P=(E\otimes_k C)\otimes_k C$, and define $p_a(e\otimes c)=(e\otimes c)\otimes1$, $p_b(e\otimes c)=\rho(e)\otimes c$, and $p_{ab}(e\otimes c)=e\otimes\Delta(c)$ with the associativity identification. For an $L$-linear isomorphism $d:L\otimes_{E,\rho}M\simeq M\otimes_k C$ and any $k$-algebra map $p:L\to A$, its pullback is the $A$-linear map $p^*d:A\otimes_{E,p\rho}M\to A\otimes_{E,pt}M$ determined as follows: for every finite presentation $d(1\otimes m)=\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i$, its value on $1\otimes m$ is $\sum_i p(1\otimes b_i)\otimes a_i$. This specifies the scalar extension of $d$ under the canonical extension comparisons, independently of the finite presentation. A linearization is such an $L$-linear isomorphism $d$ for which $u_L^*d$ is the identity of $M$ and $p_a^*d\circ p_b^*d=p_{ab}^*d$. The identity pullback uses the source and target identifications $E\otimes_{E,u_L\rho}M\simeq M$ and $E\otimes_{E,u_Lt}M\simeq M$, both $e\otimes m\mapsto em$. In the cocycle, the source transport identifies $P\otimes_{E,p_b\rho}M$ with $P\otimes_{E,p_{ab}\rho}M$, the middle transport identifies $P\otimes_{E,p_bt}M$ with $P\otimes_{E,p_a\rho}M$, and the target transport identifies $P\otimes_{E,p_at}M$ with $P\otimes_{E,p_{ab}t}M$; every transport sends $a\otimes m$ to $a\otimes m$. These exist by the algebra coaction identities. All the maps and transports are uniquely specified by these generator formulas. Finally the coefficient multiplication map $(M\otimes_k C)\otimes_k(N\otimes_k C)\to(M\otimes_E N)\otimes_k C$ sends $(m\otimes c)\otimes(n\otimes d)$ to $(m\otimes n)\otimes cd$. These are definitions using the actual balanced tensor products, with no finite-generation or nonzero-module restriction.
